input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based termination rights (material breach 9.1, insolvency 9.2, security/SLA/law/IP 9.3) and Section 9.5 scoping; the only other exits are event-driven (6.2 failed acceptance, 19.4 warranty, 27.3 force majeure). There is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and Section 2.1 expressly denies reduction or termination rights across a three-year term (Section 8.1). Under the detection guidance, the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (missing behaviour) and sits in walk-away territory. We inserted the preferred 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, expressly denied Vendor a mid-term convenience right, and conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay commitment does not negate the new right.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; conform take-or-pay language
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since the Agreement runs three years with no exit other than for cause. We also conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay commitment does not override that right; if helpful we can discuss a longer notice period as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination fee, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis, subject to Customer's reduction and termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4.
